title: The Four Oxen and the Lion
text:
Four oxen grazed together in the same field. A lion had watched them for a long time and wanted very much to eat them, but whenever he crept close, the oxen turned their tails together and faced outward, so that from every side he met a row of horns. He could not find a way in, and he went away hungry again and again.

The lion changed his method. Instead of attacking, he began to talk. He visited one ox and hinted what the others were saying about him behind his back. He visited the next and did the same. Little by little suspicion grew among the four, until they quarreled and stopped feeding together. Each went off to graze alone in a separate corner of the field.

That was all the lion had been waiting for. He attacked them one at a time, and one at a time, with no horns guarding their backs, they fell to him until none was left.
lesson: A group that stands together is hard to beat, which is why rivals often try to divide it first. Treat whispered stories about your teammates with suspicion.
source: Aesop's Fables, The Lion and the Four Bulls (also The Lion and the Three Bulls); Avianus, Fables
